newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti moves towards equilibrium - Passera.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti moves towards equilibrium - Passera.

text.p: Olivetti's slide back to operating loss in the first half of 1996 was linked to grave mistakes made in predicting the recovery of the economy and that of the sector where the group operates, according to the company's ex-chief executive Corrado Passera.
But Passera said Olivetti had now certainly found the way to return to a stable equilibrium. He was speaking to an industrial commission of the Italian lower house of parliament.
Passera, who left Olivetti at the end of June, said group margins had declined in the period 1990-95 to 22 percent from 35 percent and to survive the group had to cut costs by 40 percent.

According to the Passera's figures, in this period Olivetti cut its workforce by 47.1 percent, more than IBM with 41 percent but not as severely as DEC, Unisys and Bull which cut their workforces between 48 and 54 percent.
Passera, was replaced by Francesco Caio in early July as chief executive, who in turn was replaced by Roberto Colaninno this month.
